Francesa Albanese, the United Nations special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories, speaks at a conference, “A Cartography of Genocide: Israel’s Conduct in Gaza,” at the Roma Tre University, in Rome, Italy, Oct. 6, 2025. Photo: REUTERS/Remo Casilli

Francesca Albanese, the United Nations’ special rapporteur on the human rights situation in the Palestinian territories, is facing backlash for calling for an end to military assistance to Ukraine and arguing the war there serves a broader geopolitical interest in keeping Europe weak.

The controversy follows remarks Albanese made on September 19 at the Festival di Open in Parma, Italy. Asked about the war in Ukraine, Albanese said that she agreed with those who believe weapons shipments to Kyiv should stop and that the conflict should instead be brought back into the political arena for talks. She acknowledged that Russia invaded Ukraine and described the invasion as illegitimate, while arguing that there were broader political and geopolitical factors behind the conflict.

Albanese, who has a mandate from the UN to advise the international body on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, acknowledged last week that she did not have a solution for ending the war in Ukraine and said that she was not an expert on the conflict.

“I agree with those who believe that we need to stop sending weapons to Ukraine and bring the discussion back into the political sphere,” Albanese said.

“I don’t have the solution for ending the war,” she continued, “but I am convinced that the situation in Ukraine is being exploited to justify that horrible argument that we are already at war and that it is a hybrid war.”

The UN adviser also suggested that there was a political calculation within NATO, which she said is led by the United States, that could benefit from a weaker Europe and prolong the conflict at the cost of Ukrainian lives.

“There are a number of reasons that led to that war, but a war remains a war and it is illegitimate,” she added.

Albanese lamenting what she described as a perceived double standard in the international community’s approach to Ukraine and the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza. She argued that international institutions were much more vigorous in applying international law to the conflict in Ukraine and suggested that the lack of sanctions applied to Israel indicated unfairness in application of such laws.

“What I said from the beginning to the diplomats I met, especially those from the Western world, was that when Russia invaded Ukraine, you applied international law exactly according to the books and manuals on how to respond to aggression, from A to Z,” she said. “How is it possible that, in the face of a case that, from the standpoint of aggression, presents similarities — I’m not saying the situations are the same, but there is still an act of aggression — such as Israel’s against Palestine, the same thing is not done?”

Critics were quick to castigate Albanese for her comments.

“Russian propaganda immediately seized on Albanese’s words and her UN title to validate Moscow’s narrative,” UN Watch executive director Hillel Neuer said in a statement. “Having acknowledged Russia’s aggression, she insinuated that there were ‘reasons’ for it and then sought to deprive its victim of the means to defend itself.”

Russia Direct, which is a Russian propaganda social media account, quickly reposted Albanese’s remarks while spotlighting her position  as a UN rapporteur.

Journalist Oz Katerji slammed Albanese as someone who “apologizes” for anti-regimes in Syria, Russia, and Iran, as well as for the Lebanese terrorist group Hezbollah. “So, of course she thinks Ukraine should be cut off from arms,” he added on social media.
